test: S2 to S8: two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the per-instance differences; S1: a permutation test of the chi-square statistic of the condition by choice table, the ten choices of an instance and seat shuffled over the conditions (10,000 permutations). Holm correction over the eight hypotheses at alpha = .05. A hypothesis is confirmed when its Holm-adjusted p is below .05 and the mean difference has the stated direction. The mean difference with a bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 resamples of instances), the exact sign test and d_z are reported beside it.

hypotheses.claim: Which rule set the agent picks, when it must pick one, depends on the condition.
An agent that must pick one of the five rule sets earns more than the default agent in its seat (ten conditions).
An agent that picks its own rule set earns less than an agent assigned the collaborating rule (ten conditions).
The partner of an agent that picks its own rule set earns less than the partner of the default agent (ten conditions).

Instance by instance the agent picks rule sets that do better there: the assigned-cell payoff of the rule set it picked exceeds the average assigned-cell payoff, on the same instance and seat, of rule sets drawn with the condition's pick frequencies (ten conditions).
Two agents that each pick their own rule set reach a lower joint payoff than the default pair.
Against a competing partner, an agent that picks a rule set again before every move earns more than the default agent does against that partner.
An agent that may choose a rule set or none earns more than the default agent in its seat (ten conditions).
